text:
sam-support: heads up - ACME just opened a ticket, their embeddings endpoint vectors/sec dropped ~4x around 14:03 UTC, tokens/sec looks stable. They see 502s and occasional 429s.
acme-infra: yep, started at 14:02. We pushed a small batching rollout an hour before. No other deploys.
sam-support: can you paste a minimal failing request?
acme-infra: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1024","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_hint":128}'
devon-ml: interesting — model is a 1024-dim variant, but their payloads are varied lengths. any dimension mismatch logs?
acme-infra: no 400s for dim mismatch, but we see slow queue drain on the vectorizer side.
raj-oncall: pinging eng-sre for queue depth metrics and GPU backlog. @ingrid-sre can you check GPU queue length for the vector workers in us-west?
ingrid-sre: looking. I see GPU queue depth spike from ~40 -> 180 around 14:03 on pool vector-1024-usw. Concurrent requests rose slightly but not enough to explain 4x drop. Also saw kvcache wait times spike (avg wait 2.3s -> 18.7s).
devon-ml: kv cache waits -> could be autosplit/autobatching change causing more KV lock contention. Any rollout config changes?
acme-infra: we toggled "adaptive_batch_shrink": true in client since 13:50 (to optimize tail latency).
sam-support: could that cause more small batches and higher scheduling overhead?
devon-ml: maybe the client-side adaptive shrink is interacting badly with server-side continuous batching, producing many tiny batches that still consume GPU context switches. That explains tokens/sec OK (tokenized subrequests proceed) but vectors/sec falls because post-tokenization vectorization pipeline is bottlenecked.
raj-oncall: I pulled a trace for one request:
```
REQUEST_ID: r-0a1b2c
receive: 0.002s
tokenize: 0.014s
enqueue: wait 0.350s
batch_start: 18.532s
kv_cache_lock_wait: 16.9s
gpu_exec: 0.012s
response_sent: 18.560s
```
ingrid-sre: that kv_cache_lock_wait stands out. Could be lock thrash when many small batches try to access prefix cache.
devon-ml: hypothesis: adaptive_batch_shrink on client caused many tiny batches => more frequent KV cache hot-shard access => lock contention => GPU pipeline idles waiting on KV -> vectors/sec drops while tokens/sec (pre-KV) remain similar.
acme-infra: we can repro quickly; disabling adaptive_batch_shrink on client and forcing larger batch_hint reduces observed queue depth locally.
sam-support: can you patch them for repro steps we can run?
acme-infra: repro steps: (1) run loadtest script with 500 qps, input sizes 64-2048 tokens mix; (2) client config: adaptive_batch_shrink=true vs false; (3) monitor /internal/metrics vector_dispatch_queue, kv_cache_lock_wait, gpu_queue_depth. Script: `./tools/loadtest --qps 500 --model rwd-embed-1024 --mix small,medium,large --clients 8`.
devon-ml: thanks. On our side I'll check for any recent change in server continuous batching and KV lock implementation.
ingrid-sre: I also pulled the node logs — there were a handful of replica restarts during the spike (OOM? no, not OOM). Restart pattern: process stopped accepting batches for ~30s while kernel rebind occurred (driver level).
raj-oncall: could GPU context switching from tiny batches cause driver instability?
devon-ml: possible. Also look at kernel scheduling: tiny batches produce more kernel launches per second which may thrash the scheduler and increase driver latency.
sam-support: immediate mitigation for ACME?
ingrid-sre: two quick options: (A) ask ACME to disable adaptive_batch_shrink (client rollback) — fastest; (B) server-side temporary mitigation: increase KV cache shard concurrency and add backpressure so we coalesce tiny batches for 200ms window. I can push (B) as a config tweak to staging now, then prod if safe.
acme-infra: we'll try (A) first. Rolling back client toggle now.
acme-infra: rollback done at 14:18. Monitoring...
ingrid-sre: GPU queue depth trending down within 90s. KV cache wait median back to 1.1s.
acme-infra: vectors/sec back to baseline by 14:21. No more 502/429s.
sam-support: awesome — looks like a client-side rollout interaction. Can we capture explicit repro traces for the postmortem?
devon-ml: yes — please upload full traces and loadtest outputs to the incident folder. Also I'll open a small spike test to reproduce locally and test server-side mitigations.
raj-oncall: action items: 1) sam to update ACME ticket with repro and mitigation (client rollback) 2) devon to validate server-side KV shard concurrency change in staging 3) ingrid to add alert for kv_cache_lock_wait > 5s and gpu_queue_depth > 100 to catch this earlier.
sam-support: noted, I'll update ticket and ping account team. :thumbsup:
acme-infra: thanks all. Will keep us posted if we re-enable adaptive shrink, we want the server mitigation pathway ready.
devon-ml: follow-up: we should add guidance in the client docs recommending not to enable aggressive adaptive shrinking for high-dim embed models (>=1024) until server coalescing/backpressure is improved. I'll draft PR.
sam-support: closing this thread in slack, will attach incident summary to ticket. Great work. :clap:
